doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Paid lessons while he stepped out to take care of business
summary: Students paid for lessons in his house while he slipped out to get drugs.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: When you said you gave these guys lessons, was it informal? Formal? Come see me every week?

Oh no. They were paying me for lessons. Sometimes they’d come up, come in the house. I’d say, “Give me the money.” They pay me. I’d say, “You all sit down and warm up. I’ll be right back.” Right out the door. They say, “Aw, man.” Then I come back and give them their lesson.
Were you playing with them? Or you had to take care of business?
No, I had to get out of there for a minute and take care of my business. Then I would come back and give them their lesson.
